name: United Kingdom
genZNote: One monarch, four constituent nations, zero written single-document constitution — the UK really said 'we'll just wing it with centuries of precedent' and made it work.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Made up of four constituent nations — England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland — off the northwest coast of mainland Europe.
Capital: London, also the largest city and a major global financial centre.
Northern Ireland shares its only land border with the Republic of Ireland; the rest of the UK is surrounded by sea.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: English is the dominant language; Welsh, Scottish Gaelic, and Irish also hold official/recognised status in their respective nations.
Historic centre of English literature (Shakespeare) and the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution.
Stonehenge and the Tower of London are among its UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A parliamentary constitutional monarchy — the Monarch is head of state (a largely ceremonial role today), while the Prime Minister leads the government.
Uses an UNCODIFIED constitution — no single written document, but a body of statutes, conventions, and common law.
Bicameral Parliament: House of Commons (elected) and House of Lords (largely appointed/hereditary).
Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland each have varying degrees of devolved government.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A permanent member of the UN Security Council; a founding NATO member and member of the G7 and G20.
Head of the Commonwealth of Nations, a voluntary association of mostly former British territories, including India.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India was under British colonial rule until independence in 1947; the two countries now describe their ties as a 'Comprehensive Strategic Partnership'.
Home to a large and long-established Indian diaspora, with deep historical, cultural, and economic links.
The UK and India have negotiated a Free Trade Agreement, part of deepening post-Brexit trade ties between the two.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A services-driven economy, with London as one of the world's leading financial centres.
Left the European Union in 2020 ('Brexit'), reshaping its trade relationships with both the EU and other partners.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being the origin of the Industrial Revolution, parliamentary democracy as a governance model, and the Commonwealth of Nations.
London's status as a global financial and cultural capital.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The United Kingdom is a parliamentary constitutional monarchy of four nations, with an uncodified constitution and a former colonial relationship with India.
keyFacts: Four constituent nations: England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland.
Uncodified constitution — no single written constitutional document.
Left the EU in 2020 (Brexit); permanent UN Security Council member.
commonConfusion: The UK's constitution is UNCODIFIED (no single document) — a common exam trap, since most countries (including India) have a codified written constitution.

highYieldFacts: The UK has an uncodified constitution — one of very few major democracies without a single written constitutional document.
The UK is Head of the Commonwealth of Nations, which India is also a member of.
commonTraps: Assuming every parliamentary democracy has a single written constitution — the UK is the classic exception.
mustRemember: UK = 4 nations, uncodified constitution, permanent UNSC member, former colonial ruler of India (independence 1947).
